recognize_zh: 電子顯微鏡下一個雙核紅血球前驅細胞，兩個核大小不等、中間仍以細橋相連（不等分核出芽），核內高電子密度的異染色質呈粗大分支狀並佈滿許多小透亮孔洞，形成「瑞士起司」外觀，為 CDA type I 的特徵超微結構。
features: Transmission electron micrograph of an erythroid precursor with two unequal nuclear lobes joined by a narrow bridge
Electron-dense heterochromatin forming coarse, anastomosing bands and clumps
Numerous small electron-lucent vacuoles within the heterochromatin (Swiss cheese pattern)
Nuclear envelope largely intact; homogeneous electron-dense hemoglobinized cytoplasm
Adjacent red cells at edges of the field
describe_en: Transmission electron microscopy of a bone marrow erythroid precursor shows a binucleated or bilobed cell with nuclear portions of unequal size connected by a narrow chromatin bridge. The heterochromatin is abnormally condensed into coarse, branching electron-dense masses riddled with small electron-lucent holes, producing a spongy Swiss cheese appearance. The cytoplasm is moderately electron dense, consistent with hemoglobinization. Findings are consistent with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.

ddx.vs: CDA II shows peripheral double membranes of endoplasmic reticulum parallel to the cell membrane on EM rather than spongy heterochromatin, with binucleated late normoblasts and a positive acidified serum test.
Megaloblastic precursors show open, sieve-like chromatin with nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony but not the Swiss cheese heterochromatin or internuclear bridges.
MDS shows nuclear budding and ring sideroblasts in adults with clonal cytogenetic or mutational abnormalities, not the congenital CDAN1/CDIN1-related heterochromatin defect.
